findings.title: Many truth_frames/roster source fields are not mapped and some silently dropped (beyond the author's declared gap list)
findings.detail: Per-frame entity rows carry ~30 fields; canonical frame records keep only 6 (pose.position/velocity/yaw, speed, activity_type, visibility_state). Frame-level fields (active_roi_id, active_site_id, capture_boundary_id, entity_motion_state, inspect_observes_boundary, map_id, pad_boundary_policy, render_mode, roster_summary, sumo_active_incidents, sumo_segment, sumo_semantics, sumo_traffic_light_states, uav_crosses_boundary, uav_global_flow, uav_segment) and entity-level fields (state, entity_type, label_class, role, task_id, site_id, roi_id, route_waypoints_enu_m, runtime_visibility, semantic_role, background_role, tags, state_sequence, state_revision, visual_revision, activation_tick, ground_flow_contract, contract_scenario_id, logical_asset_id, proxy_template_id, plus annotations.state_facets and render_presence.offstage/offstage_reason/roi_membership/submission_state/global_roster) have no canonical family. Roster keeps 3 of ~25 fields. Event source records carry 27 keys; canonical event keeps 5 (start_tick, trigger_predicate_id/trigger_tick, event_level, source_class, continuity_status, event_phases, supporting_* all dropped). This is a broader set than author_result's open_dependencies_and_gaps list, which names compute/communication/domain_state/receiver-log families but not these truth-side fields.
findings.impact: S01.02's requirement to import 'all states, relations and observation paths' from one episode is met only for the pilot-selected subset; the stop-threshold wording (real field misses must not be papered over with UNKNOWN) is respected - nothing is masked - but the mapping is not complete and the residual list in author_result.json understates it.

findings.title: All 4 delta operation kinds are collapsed into one edge record shape; refresh_predicate_evidence dominates (130152/138831) and its evidence/observation payload is dropped
findings.detail: refresh ops carry observations, source_refs, missing_source_record, binding_ontology_classes - none are canonicalized; relation.value is 'true'/'false'/'unknown'/'out_of_scope' for refresh records, so a refresh of an assertion is indistinguishable at canonical level from an add. remove_predicate_assertion ops have only from_value, which the importer falls back to as relation.value (3565 records), so a removal is stored with the value it had before removal; nothing marks the record as a removal except source.operation. add ops carry binding_provenance/ontology_argument_roles/evidence_update_tick/truth_state_update_tick - dropped.
findings.impact: lossy for relation-layer consumers: the canonical edge stream alone cannot rebuild the graph's assertion state at a tick without reading source.operation from the provenance dict, and evidence-side semantics (why a value is believed) are lost. For the S01.02 acceptance question ('canonical record returns to the exact source operation') provenance still works, but canonical-layer completeness is reduced.

findings.title: Spec negative 'illegal unit' is not actually detected by the schema
findings.detail: Spec requires the schema to recognize an illegal unit as a counterexample. The only unit check in code is that UNIT_DIMENSIONS exists and is exported into the contract document; validate_value never consults it. Registering a family with unit 'furlongs_per_fortnight' succeeds, the contract document happily carries it, and validation passes silently.
findings.repro: from p01v4.contracts import schema as S; S.FIELD_FAMILIES['probe.bad_unit']=S._f('real','furlongs_per_fortnight',records=('frame',)); S.validate_value('probe.bad_unit',1.0,'p',record_kind='frame') -> no error; S.schema_document()['field_families']['probe.bad_unit']['unit']=='furlongs_per_fortnight'
findings.verdict: add a unit-membership check in _f or validate_value; the fixture 'illegal_unit_family' case actually tests frame mixing, not units, so the suite does not cover this spec negative

findings.title: Two negatives are self-fulfilling: duplicate-id and truncation tests never exercise the production path
findings.detail: test_schema.py test_duplicate_entity_id_detected re-implements the duplicate check inline (raises SchemaError from the test body) instead of calling CanonicalEpisode.add(check_id=True). test_import_episode.py test_truncated_history_detected manually removes tick 450 from the report's tick list and then appends the expected error string into report.errors by hand; neither the importer's gap check nor add()'s id index runs.
findings.verdict: rewrite both to call the real API; the underlying production behavior is correct (verified independently by this review), so this is test-only remediation

findings.title: Compact encoding has two exact-roundtrip collisions between present values and structural markers
findings.detail: (a) A present string cell beginning with '!' (e.g. annotations.activity_type='!missing') encodes to the same '!missing' cell as the non-present marker and decodes as kind=missing. (b) A present object cell exactly {'f':...,'v':...} (e.g. relation.bindings={'f':'N','v':'x'}) encodes to the frame-tagged vector cell and decodes as {'frame':'N','value':'x'}. Both are silent information changes. The pilot episode contains zero colliding cells (verified), so no measured artifact is corrupted today; the risk is for future source data and for decode-side drift.
findings.repro: python - SE.encode_compact([{'record_kind':'frame','id':'fa','tick':1,'fields':{'annotations.activity_type':'!missing'}}]) then decode_compact -> {'kind':'missing'}; same with bindings {'f':'N','v':'x'} -> {'frame':'N','value':'x'}
findings.verdict: tag non-present cells unambiguously (e.g. {'kind':...} wrapper or escaping) or document the collision as a declared encoding boundary with a validation-time rejection of '!'-prefixed strings

findings.title: source_family/split_group machinery exists but is not wired into supervision-window construction
findings.detail: provenance.split_group requires a caller-supplied split_table loaded from a versioned config; no such config artifact exists in the results root (configs/ has only serialization.json and pilot-windows.json), windows.build_supervision_window/SupervisionSample carry no split_group/source_family field, and SupervisionSample.split remains a free-form caller string. The SPLIT_TABLE lives only inside the test module. Consequence: the coupling rule ('every window of one source shares one split; versions are not independent examples') is enforced only in tests, not by the data path that actually builds training samples; a caller can still construct a sample with split='TEST' on a TRAIN source without any error.
findings.repro: grep split_group in src/p01v4/data/windows.py -> no match; call W.build_supervision_window(records, split='TEST', ...) -> succeeds
findings.verdict: wire split_group into build_supervision_window (validate the sample split against the table for the episode's original key) and persist a versioned split-table config in the results root

findings.title: scan_input_leak's second guard is dead code; leak rejection for smuggled future content rests on the tick check alone
findings.detail: In windows.py scan_input_leak, the 'future pose / caption payloads must never be copied into input-branch records' branch re-tests the same condition as the first branch (record_kind=='frame' and tick>cutoff) and is therefore unreachable after the first check. The meaningful case - a future payload (pose/caption/visibility values) placed in a record whose tick is <= cutoff - is not detectable from a single record's tick and is only addressed by the new audit_input_selector (perturbation audit), which the builder does not call by default. In the shipped pipeline the builder assigns records by tick, so the invariant holds by construction; the guard is documentation-grade rather than a control.
findings.verdict: either remove the dead branch or make the builder run audit_input_selector on the input predicate; not a correctness bug for the pilot path

result_rationale: The four declared S01.01-S01.04 suites reproduce green with real source equivalence, correct cutoff/fit discipline, exact round-trip on pilot data, and honest provenance; the parent six-point supplement is implemented in code with passing tests. However five concrete items block a clean preliminary acceptance: an unimplemented spec negative (illegal unit, F3), canonical-layer relation semantics loss beyond the declared gap list (F1/F2), a split-coupling rule that exists only in tests rather than the data path (F6), and two self-fulfilling negative tests (F4); the compact-marker collision (F5) should be fixed or explicitly declared as an encoding boundary. All are bounded, code-level remediations; none require re-architecture or new data.
